summary: G-banded chromosome analysis of an unstimulated bone marrow aspirate (24- and 48-hour synchronized cultures; 20 cells counted, 5 karyotyped; 400-425 bphs) showed a normal male karyotype, 46,XY[20], with no clonal numerical or structural abnormality at the stated band resolution. Interphase FISH using the acute myeloid leukemia panel (200 nuclei scored per probe) was negative for RUNX1-RUNX1T1, CBFB, PML-RARA, KMT2A (MLL), MECOM (EVI1), -5/5q- (EGR1), -7/7q- (D7S486), and TP53 (17p13.1) deletion, with all signal counts within the laboratory's normal cutoff range. The report interprets the case as cytogenetically normal, states that a normal karyotype does not exclude a submicroscopic abnormality, and states that molecular testing (NPM1, FLT3, CEBPA, and a broader myeloid panel) is required for classification and risk stratification and has been ordered separately (accession MMD-26-NGS-22150).

stated_limitations: The report states that a normal karyotype does not exclude a submicroscopic abnormality and that correlation with FISH and molecular studies is advised. Results apply at the stated band resolution (400-425 bphs), with 20 cells counted and 5 fully karyotyped. Cytogenetically normal AML is described as frequently driven by gene-level mutations not visible by karyotype or FISH; molecular testing (NPM1, FLT3, CEBPA, and a broader myeloid panel) is stated to be required for classification and risk stratification and has been ordered separately (accession MMD-26-NGS-22150). The report is one component of a combined hematopathology workup and should be interpreted together with the morphology, flow cytometry, and molecular reports.
